blocks.text: Under the TRIPS agreement, Australia is obliged to provide a mechanism for the protection of Geographic Indications (GIs) in Australia. There are two ways to protect GIs in Australia:
registration of the GI as a certification trade mark

protection of GIs for wine or grape products through the provisions of the Wine Australia Act 2013. More information on this can be found in Part 32B – Examination of Trade Marks for Wine (in Class 33).
Section 6 of the Act defines a GI in relation to goods as:

a sign that identifies the goods as originating in a country, or in a region or locality in that country, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic of the goods is essentially attributable to their geographical origin.

2.2 Registration of GIs as certification trade marks

The certification trade mark provisions are the principal way to protect a GI in Australia. As with other certification trade marks, GIs must meet the requirements of the Act relating to certification trade marks.
TEQUILA (1377413) is an example of a GI protected in Australia by registration as a certification trade mark.
